summary: The statement and proof are correct. The smallest dimension and points on facets or bin boundaries do not yield counterexamples: equal floor coordinates always give strict bounds on the corresponding barycentric differences, and choosing the sign of the omitted difference places the lattice difference strictly inside the simplex. The unique-interior-point assumption then proves injectivity for the complete lattice support and for every choice of omitted coordinate. The stated real tilt has exactly the claimed exponential expression; injectivity and finiteness give the strict comparison with the positive geometric series. The calibration simplex has precisely the asserted interior lattice point, its complete support is in bijection with the stated weak compositions, and permutation symmetry proves the zero mean needed to establish its exact capacity. The binomial coefficient bound and the root limit follow as written, proving that no smaller uniform exponential base is possible. No external result or predecessor fact is needed.
